delta_control.creating_delta_note: First cycle for all three components, so each delta is taken against an empty document: 0.0.0 -> 1.0.0, creates_document true. Same resolution as the HLD deltas.
delta_control.scope_boundary: Classes, sequence diagrams and error handling. Entity ownership, classification and retention are the data viewpoint's; a change to any of them is a data-architecture delta, not an LLD one. Two candidates surfaced here and were escalated rather than absorbed — see LLD-F01 and LLD-F02.

changes.content: RegistrationService — submit(command) -> RegistrationId; resolveStatus(producerId) -> EligibilityDecision. TokenValidator — validate(rawToken) -> Principal | TokenRejected. RoleProvisioner — provision(principal, onboardingRecord) -> Role. FboRegisterClient — lookup(fboNumber) -> Verified | Invalid | NoAnswer. ProducerRepository — append-only over identity_schema; supersede(registration) rather than update(registration).

```text
producer-portal -> RegistrationService : POST /v1/producers/registrations
RegistrationService -> RegistrationService : validate fbo_number format
RegistrationService -> RegistrationService : assert fbo_attestation == true   [server-side]
RegistrationService -> ProducerRepository : append Producer + FoodSafetyRegistration
                                            status = pending-verification
RegistrationService --> producer-portal : 201 Created { registrationId }
RegistrationService -> FboRegisterClient : lookup(fbo_number)   [async, out of band]
```

```text
FboRegisterClient -> competent-authority register : lookup
alt Verified
    FboRegisterClient -> ProducerRepository : append FoodSafetyRegistration
                                              status = valid, supersedes prior row
    FboRegisterClient -> EventPublisher      : identity.registration.verified
else Invalid
    FboRegisterClient -> ProducerRepository : append status = rejected, reason passed through
    FboRegisterClient -> EventPublisher      : identity.registration.verified (outcome=rejected)
else NoAnswer
    FboRegisterClient -> RetryScheduler      : schedule bounded retry
    note: no row appended, no event emitted, status stays pending-verification
end
```

Malformed fbo_number -> 400 with a field-level problem detail; no row appended (S-F1.1-a-AC2). Missing attestation -> 422; refused server-side regardless of what the client sent (S-F1.1-a-AC3, ES1). FBO register non-answer -> NoAnswer, bounded retry with exponential backoff, registration stays pending; it is never promoted to valid on a timeout, and no 'assume valid' branch exists in the code path at all (S-F1.1-b-AC3). FBO register returns Invalid -> rejected, and the register's reason string is stored and passed through verbatim, never paraphrased.

FoodSafetyRegistration rows are append-only. A status change is a new row superseding the prior one; ProducerRepository exposes no update path for this entity, so 'supersede, never overwrite' is enforced by the absence of a method rather than by a code-review convention. The deduplication key for the emitted event is (producer_id, fbo_number, verified_on) — the business act, not the message id, which a producer's retry would regenerate.

resolveStatus(producerId) returns the latest non-superseded FoodSafetyRegistration row for that producer, ordered by appended_at. This satisfies getRegistrationStatus's p95 <= 250 ms budget only with an index on (producer_id, appended_at desc) — see LLD-F01.

RegistrationForm — local field validation, submit handler. RegistrationStatusView — polls getRegistrationStatus; no Work Unit builds it (HLD-F02). ApiClient — gateway-only, carries the session correlation id on every call.

400 -> render the field-level problem detail against the FBO field and preserve the entered value. 422 -> render the attestation requirement; the client guard is re-shown but is not treated as the control. Network failure on submit -> the form is not cleared and the submission is not retried automatically; a silent retry could create a second registration the producer never intended.

RegistrationStatusView polls at a fixed interval with no countdown and no progress indication. The view cannot distinguish a slow lookup from a timed-out one and must not imply it can (S-F1.1-b-AC3, wireframes WF-02).

VerificationOutcomeNotifier — handle(event) with a DedupStore lookup on (producer_id, fbo_number, verified_on) before any send. TemplateRenderer — renders from the event payload only; has no read path to identity_schema, which would breach DAT-1.b.

Duplicate delivery -> DedupStore hit, no send, acknowledged. Render failure -> dead-letter with the named owner, never discarded: the verification really happened, and a dropped evidence-derived notification is a producer who was never told their livelihood is blocked. Mail transport failure -> bounded retry, then dead-letter. No replay path exists — the source event is Evidence kind and a replay would re-assert the fact.

findings.summary: Append-only evidence plus a 250 ms status read implies an index the data architecture has not been asked for.
findings.detail: DAT-3.2 makes FoodSafetyRegistration append-only, so current status is the latest non-superseded row rather than a column. INT-4.3 budgets the status read at p95 <= 250 ms. Meeting that over an append-only history needs an index on (producer_id, appended_at desc), and as row counts grow it may need a current-status projection.
findings.resolution_note: Not decided here. An index is physical schema and belongs to the data architecture delta; a projection would be a registered read model with a staleness budget under DAT-6, which is emphatically not an LLD's to invent. The LLD states the access pattern and the budget it has to meet, and stops.

findings.summary: The register's reason string is stored, and no classification covers it.
findings.detail: LLD-4 stores the competent authority's rejection reason verbatim so it can be passed through unparaphrased. That string is a new stored value on a Regulated Evidence entity and could carry identifying or commercially sensitive content. DAT-3.2 classifies the entity, not this field.
findings.resolution_note: Raised for the data architecture delta. The LLD does not assign a classification, because assigning one here would put a governance decision in a class diagram.

findings.summary: The 'no assume-valid branch' rule is a design assertion with no test that can prove its absence.
findings.detail: LLD-4 states that no code path promotes a pending registration to valid on a timeout. TC-S-F1.1-b-03 proves the timeout leaves it pending, which is evidence of the behaviour but not of the absence of the branch.
findings.resolution_note: Flagged for the adversarial case writer: the useful case is a register that answers with a malformed or ambiguous payload, where an optimistic branch would be most tempting to add later.

consistency_check.note: Class responsibilities were checked against the HLD components they realise, and every error path against the acceptance criterion it serves. One correction during authoring: ProducerRepository was drafted with an update(registration) method, which contradicts DAT-3.2's append-only rule. Replaced with supersede(registration), so the prohibition is enforced by the absence of a method rather than by convention.

artifacts.name: lld-identity-service.delta.json
artifacts.description: Creating delta 0.0.0 -> 1.0.0, 6 sections including two sequence diagrams

content.execution_summary:
• Emitted 3 LLD deltas — identity-service, producer-portal, notifications-worker — all creating (0.0.0 -> 1.0.0), all additive, none structural, no ADR.
• Two sequence diagrams carry the cycle's real behaviour: registration submission, and the three-way verification outcome. The NoAnswer branch is the one worth reading — it appends no row, emits no event and leaves the registration pending, and LLD-4 states that no 'assume valid' path exists in the code at all rather than merely that it is not taken.
• Two design decisions are enforced structurally rather than by convention. ProducerRepository exposes supersede() and no update(), so DAT-3.2's append-only rule cannot be broken by a well-meaning edit — this was a correction during authoring, the draft had update(). And TemplateRenderer renders from the event payload only, with no read path to identity_schema, so DAT-1.b holds by construction in notifications-worker.
• Three findings, two of them escalated to the data architect rather than absorbed. LLD-F01 is the substantive one: append-only evidence plus a 250 ms status read implies an index, and possibly a current-status projection — an index is physical schema and a projection would be a DAT-6 registered read model with a staleness budget. Neither is an LLD's to invent, so the LLD states the access pattern and the budget and stops. LLD-F02 notes the register's rejection reason is a newly stored string on a Regulated Evidence entity that no classification covers.
• LLD-F03 flags a limit of the current test set for the adversarial case writer: TC-S-F1.1-b-03 proves a timeout leaves the registration pending, which is evidence of behaviour, not of the absence of an optimistic branch. The case worth writing is a malformed or ambiguous register response.
• Knowledge bases consulted: kb-L1-enterprise-architecture (component boundaries); kb-L2-food-domain via the integration architecture (FD3 evidence-event semantics, FD4 refusal on unknown eligibility, FD7 deduplication from the business act).
• Guardrails evaluated: gr-L1-consistency-check (pass — one correction, the removed update() method).
